> **Pipeline step 03 — gear check (supporting).**
>
> **Purpose.** Tests whether the two TPS trawl gears (Mamou vs otter) differ in catch or in
> measured fork length once the model covariates are accounted for, on the subset of tows where
> both gears were fished, and produces the gear-comparison figures.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv`, `data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv`,
> `data/tps_forklength_data.csv`.
>
> **Outputs.** fits in `fits_gear_compare/`; figures `output_figs/gear_*`.
>
> (The covariate-correlation matrices that used to sit in section 7 of this notebook now live in
> `04_diagnostics/covariate_correlations_by_water_year.Rmd`.)

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
Does gear type affect catch of sub-75 mm Chinook, after accounting for the
predictors that showed a clear effect in the main catch models?

Model formula follows the most recently graphed TPS catch models
(`tidal-parr-trawl-analysis2_kfold.Rmd`, `build_station_formula()`):
`n_l_75 ~ <fixef> + s(water_year_day) + offset(log(Volume)) + (1|StationCode)`,
negative binomial, with `catch_priors`. Here `<fixef>` is `Gear + out30_z +
Edge_Type`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(brms)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

FIT_DIR <- "fits_gear_compare"
dir.create(FIT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)
force_refit <- FALSE   # TRUE to re-run all fits from scratch
```

# 1. Build the paired subset

Start from `tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv` -- the same modeling frame the graphed
catch models used -- so `out30_z`, `water_year_day` and `Edge_Type` are
constructed identically rather than re-derived here.

```{r load}
tps <- read.csv("data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv") %>%
  mutate(date = mdy(SampleDate),
         wk   = isoweek(date),
         yrwk = paste0(year(date), "-W", sprintf("%02d", wk)))

table(tps$Gear, tps$water_year)
```

**The Otter net was only ever fished in WY2019** (Jan 23 - May 17, 2019), so the
comparison is automatically confined to that season. Restrict to weeks in which
*both* gears were fished:

```{r subset}
paired <- tps %>%
  filter(Gear %in% c("Mamou", "Otter")) %>%
  group_by(yrwk) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(Gear) == 2) %>%     # keep only weeks where both were fished
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Gear      = factor(Gear, levels = c("Mamou", "Otter")),  # Mamou = reference
         Edge_Type = factor(Edge_Type),
         yrwk      = factor(yrwk))

table(paired$yrwk, paired$Gear)
```

```{r raw-cpue}
paired %>%
  group_by(Gear) %>%
  summarise(tows = n(), zeros = sum(n_l_75 == 0), positive = sum(n_l_75 > 0),
            catch = sum(n_l_75), volume = sum(Volume),
            CPUE_per_10k_m3 = sum(n_l_75) / sum(Volume) * 10000, .groups = "drop")
```

# 2. Balance check: what else differs between the gears?

This is the part that decides how much the model can be trusted, so look before
fitting.

```{r balance}
paired %>%
  group_by(Gear) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            median_volume        = round(median(Volume)),
            median_dist_channel  = round(median(DistanceAlongChannel)),
            median_dist_m        = round(median(Distance_m)),
            .groups = "drop")

table(paired$Edge_Type, paired$Gear)
table(paired$habitat2020, paired$Gear)

# were the two gears ever fished at the same location?
loc <- paired %>% mutate(loc = paste(round(Station_Latitude, 4),
                                     round(Station_Longitude, 4)))
tab <- table(loc$loc, loc$Gear)
sprintf("locations fished by BOTH gears: %d of %d", sum(tab[,1] > 0 & tab[,2] > 0), nrow(tab))
```

Three things matter here:

1. **No location was fished by both gears** (0 of 160). This is a *temporally*
   paired design, not a spatially paired one -- the gears were used in the same
   weeks but at different sites. Any site-level difference is therefore
   confounded with gear.
2. Otter tows sit further down-channel and closer to the channel axis than
   Mamou tows (median `DistanceAlongChannel` ~16,600 vs ~21,000 m).
   `habitat2020` and `Edge_Type` are also unbalanced -- Emergent Vegetation is
   5 Mamou vs 20 Otter.
3. Within a single water year `out30_z` is a deterministic function of date
   (16 distinct outflow values over 16 sampling dates), so it is **functionally
   confounded with `s(water_year_day)`** -- a flexible smooth of day can
   reproduce the outflow trajectory exactly. Expect the outflow coefficient to
   be weakly identified. This does *not* threaten the gear contrast, because
   both gears were fished within the same weeks.

Because there are only 16 unique sampling dates, the smooth basis is capped at
`k = 5`; the brms default `k = 10` is over-flexible for 16 distinct x-values
and would soak up between-week variation that the gear term should be competing
against.

# 3. Models

`catch_priors` copied verbatim from `tidal-parr-trawl-analysis2_kfold.Rmd`.

```{r priors}
catch_priors <- c(prior(normal(0, 2.5),  class = "b"),
                  prior(gamma(2, 0.1),   class = "shape"),
                  prior(normal(-5.5, 2), class = "Intercept"),
                  prior(normal(20, 5),   class = "sds"))

fit_cached <- function(name, formula, data, priors = catch_priors, ...) {
  path <- file.path(FIT_DIR, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  if (!force_refit && file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  fit <- brm(formula = formula, family = negbinomial(link = "log"),
             data = data, prior = priors,
             iter = 3000, warmup = 2000, chains = 4,
             control = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99),
             save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE), ...)
  saveRDS(fit, path)
  fit
}
```

```{r fl-fit-helper}
# gaussian counterpart of fit_cached(), for the fork-length models in section 8
fit_cached_fl <- function(name, formula, data, priors = fl_priors, ...) {
  path <- file.path(FIT_DIR, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  if (!force_refit && file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  fit <- brm(formula = formula, family = gaussian(),
             data = data, prior = priors,
             iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, chains = 4,
             control = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99),
             save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE), ...)
  saveRDS(fit, path); fit
}
```

## M1 -- as specified

Matches the graphed catch-model structure, with `Gear` added.

Note `(1|StationCode)` is an *observation-level* random effect here: TPS
StationCodes are unique per tow (`TPS0123.2019`), so there is one level per row.
That is also true of the graphed models, so it is kept for consistency, but it
is competing with the negative-binomial `shape` for the same overdispersion.

```{r m1}
m1 <- fit_cached("m1_requested",
  n_l_75 ~ Gear + out30_z + Edge_Type + s(water_year_day, k = 5) +
           offset(log(Volume)) + (1 | StationCode),
  data = paired)
summary(m1)
```

## M2 -- within-week contrast (recommended)

This is the answer to "how do I make sure I only compare paired gear from the
same time period". Rather than modelling calendar time with a smooth and hoping
it lines up, make **week the unit of pairing**: a random intercept for `yrwk`
absorbs everything shared by tows in the same week -- outflow, tide stage, fish
abundance, run timing -- and the `Gear` coefficient is then estimated *within*
weeks. It is the design-based version of the comparison, and it drops the
outflow/day confounding entirely because neither term is needed.

```{r m2}
m2 <- fit_cached("m2_within_week",
  n_l_75 ~ Gear + Edge_Type + offset(log(Volume)) + (1 | yrwk),
  data = paired,
  priors = c(prior(normal(0, 2.5),  class = "b"),
             prior(gamma(2, 0.1),   class = "shape"),
             prior(normal(-5.5, 2), class = "Intercept"),
             prior(exponential(1),  class = "sd")))
summary(m2)
```

## M3 -- M1 plus spatial covariates (sensitivity)

Since the gears were fished at different places, add the spatial terms from the
main model set to see whether the gear estimate moves.

```{r m3}
m3 <- fit_cached("m3_spatial",
  n_l_75 ~ Gear + out30_z + Edge_Type + distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z +
           s(water_year_day, k = 5) + offset(log(Volume)) + (1 | StationCode),
  data = paired)
summary(m3)
```

# 4. The gear effect across models

`Gear` is coded with Mamou as the reference, so `b_GearOtter` is the log rate
ratio of Otter to Mamou at equal volume. Exponentiated, 1.0 means "no gear
effect".

```{r gear-effect}
gear_rr <- function(fit, label) {
  dr <- as_draws_df(fit)$b_GearOtter
  tibble(model = label,
         RR_median = median(exp(dr)),
         RR_lo95   = quantile(exp(dr), 0.025),
         RR_hi95   = quantile(exp(dr), 0.975),
         P_Otter_gt_Mamou = mean(dr > 0))
}

bind_rows(
  gear_rr(m1, "M1: out30 + edge +\n 1|site + s(day)"),
  gear_rr(m2, "M2: out30 + edge +\n 1|week"),
  gear_rr(m3, "M3: out30 + edge +\n dist_along + dist_off + 1|site + s(day)")
) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3)))
```



# 5. Posterior predictive checks

```{r ppc, fig.width=7, fig.height=3}
pp_check(m1, type = "rootogram") + ggtitle("M1")
pp_check(m2, type = "rootogram") + ggtitle("M2")
```

# 6. Summary figures

```{r fig-setup, message=FALSE}
library(patchwork)
library(tidybayes)

GEAR_COLS <- c(Mamou = "#2E6F9E", Otter = "#C1663A")   # colourblind-safe pair
FIG <- "output_figs/gear_efficiency_mamou_vs_otter"

# Axis titles and tick labels fixed at 8 pt (journal minimum). Panel titles and
# subtitles are left larger on purpose -- they are reference text for writing
# captions and get cropped out of the final supplemental figure.
base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.title       = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text        = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text      = element_text(size = 8),   # matched to the axis text
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
        plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey30"),
        legend.position  = "top",
        legend.title     = element_blank(),
        legend.key.size  = unit(3, "mm"))
theme_set(base_theme)
```

## Panel A -- sampling design

Which weeks each gear was fished, and how many tows. Only weeks with both gears
enter the analysis.

```{r panel-a}
wk_all <- tps %>%
  filter(Gear %in% c("Mamou", "Otter"), water_year == 2019) %>%
  count(yrwk, Gear) %>%
  complete(yrwk, Gear, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(yrwk) %>%
  mutate(both = all(n > 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

pA <- ggplot(wk_all, aes(n, yrwk, fill = Gear)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = distinct(wk_all, yrwk, both) %>% filter(!both),
            aes(x = max(wk_all$n) * 1.03, y = yrwk, label = "week excluded"),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 2.3,
            colour = "grey45", fontface = "italic") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GEAR_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.30))) +
  labs(title = "A. Sampling design, WY2019",
       subtitle = "Otter was fished only in WY2019;\n 8 of 13 weeks have both gears",
       x = "Tows", y = NULL)
pA
```

## Panel B -- raw CPUE, paired within week

The within-week contrast M2 estimates, shown directly. Lines join the two gears
in the same week.

```{r panel-b}
wk_cpue <- paired %>%
  group_by(yrwk, Gear) %>%
  summarise(cpue = sum(n_l_75) / sum(Volume) * 10000, tows = n(), .groups = "drop")

pooled <- paired %>%
  group_by(Gear) %>%
  summarise(cpue = sum(n_l_75) / sum(Volume) * 10000, .groups = "drop")

pB <- ggplot(wk_cpue, aes(Gear, cpue)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = yrwk), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Gear, size = tows), alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_point(data = pooled, aes(fill = Gear), shape = 23, size = 3.4,
             colour = "black", stroke = 0.6, inherit.aes = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GEAR_COLS, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GEAR_COLS, guide = "none") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.4, 4), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "B. Raw CPUE paired by week",
       subtitle = "Grey lines join the same week; point size = tows;\n diamonds = pooled CPUE",
       x = NULL, y = expression("Catch < 75 mm per 10,000 m"^3))
pB
```

## Panel C -- what else differs between the gears

The confounding to keep in mind: no location was fished by both gears, so
habitat and position differ systematically.

```{r panel-c, fig.width=7, fig.height=3}
edge_bal <- paired %>%
  count(Gear, Edge_Type) %>%
  group_by(Gear) %>% mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()

pC1 <- ggplot(edge_bal, aes(prop, fct_rev(Edge_Type), fill = Gear)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GEAR_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(title = "C. Covariate imbalance", subtitle = "Edge type",
       x = "Share of tows", y = NULL)

pC2 <- ggplot(paired, aes(DistanceAlongChannel / 1000, Gear, fill = Gear)) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(adjust = 0.8, width = 0.7, .width = 0.5,
                       point_size = 1.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GEAR_COLS, guide = "none") +
  labs(subtitle = "Position along channel", x = "Distance along channel (km)", y = NULL)

pC <- pC1 / pC2 + plot_layout(heights = c(1.3, 1))
pC
```

## Panel D -- the gear effect

Posterior rate ratio, Otter relative to Mamou at equal towed volume.

```{r panel-d}
rr_draws <- bind_rows(
  tibble(model = "M1: out30 + edge +\n 1|site + s(day)", rr = exp(as_draws_df(m1)$b_GearOtter)),
  tibble(model = "M2: out30 + edge +\n 1|week",          rr = exp(as_draws_df(m2)$b_GearOtter)),
  tibble(model = "M3: out30 + edge +\n dist_along + dist_off +\n 1|site + s(day)", rr = exp(as_draws_df(m3)$b_GearOtter))
) %>% mutate(model = fct_rev(fct_inorder(model)))

pD <- ggplot(rr_draws, aes(rr, model)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 2, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.6) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), fill = "#7F9CB5", point_size = 1.8,
               interval_size_range = c(0.5, 1.2)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 4),        # 0.25 dropped: collides
                labels = c("0.1", "0.5", "1", "2", "4")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.08, 5)) +
  labs(title = "D. Otter : Mamou catch rate ratio",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = no gear effect;\n shaded band = within 2-fold",
       x = "Rate ratio (log scale)", y = NULL)
pD
```

## Panel E -- model-adjusted CPUE by gear

Counterfactual standardisation: predict every tow in the paired set as if it had
been fished with each gear, holding volume at 10,000 m^3, then average over the
observed covariate distribution. This removes the Edge_Type / position imbalance
that the raw CPUE in Panel B carries.

```{r panel-e}
adj_cpue <- function(fit, label) {
  map_dfr(c("Mamou", "Otter"), function(g) {
    nd <- paired %>% mutate(Gear = factor(g, levels = levels(paired$Gear)),
                            Volume = 10000)
    ep <- posterior_epred(fit, newdata = nd, re_formula = NA)   # draws x tows
    tibble(model = label, Gear = g, cpue = rowMeans(ep))        # avg over tows
  })
}

adj <- bind_rows(adj_cpue(m1, "M1"), adj_cpue(m2, "M2"), adj_cpue(m3, "M3")) %>%
  mutate(Gear = factor(Gear, levels = c("Mamou", "Otter")))

pE <- ggplot(adj, aes(cpue, model, fill = Gear)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = 0.95, point_size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), slab_alpha = 0.7,
               key_glyph = "rect") +   # match the bar panels so legends merge into one
  scale_fill_manual(values = GEAR_COLS) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 6)) +
  labs(title = "E. Model-adjusted CPUE",
       subtitle = expression("Predicted catch < 75 mm per 10,000 m"^3*" \n averaged over observed covariates"),
       x = expression("Predicted CPUE per 10,000 m"^3*" (x-axis clipped at 6)"), y = NULL)
pE
```

```{r adj-table}
adj %>% group_by(model, Gear) %>%
  summarise(median = median(cpue), lo95 = quantile(cpue, .025),
            hi95 = quantile(cpue, .975), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3)))
```

```{r combined, fig.width=9, fig.height=10}
pC2b <- pC2 + labs(subtitle = "C2. Position along channel")
# pE's halfeye keys are drawn with alpha, so ggplot won't merge them with the bar

gear_fig <- (pA | pB) / (pC1b | pC2b) / (pD | pEb) +

  theme(legend.position = "top")

gear_fig <- gear_fig +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Mamou vs Otter trawl efficiency, TPS WY2019",
    subtitle = "Sub-75 mm Chinook catch, 161 tows across 8 weeks in which both gears were fished",
    caption = "No location was fished by both gears: the design is paired in time, not in space.",
    theme = theme(plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),

gear_fig
```

```{r save-figs}
# ---- output geometry -------------------------------------------------------
COL_MM  <- 84     # single-column max width (each panel, for the supplement)
FULL_MM <- 174    # double-column width for the 2 x 3 combined figure; at this
                  # width each sub-panel lands at ~87 mm, so the 8 pt type
                  # renders at the same physical size as the standalone panels
DPI     <- 600

save_fig <- function(plot, file, width_mm, height_mm, preview = FALSE) {
  ggsave(paste0(file, ".pdf"),  plot, device = "pdf",
         width = width_mm, height = height_mm, units = "mm")
  ggsave(paste0(file, ".tiff"), plot, device = "tiff", dpi = DPI,
         compression = "lzw",
         width = width_mm, height = height_mm, units = "mm")
  if (preview)
    ggsave(paste0(file, "_preview.png"), plot, device = "png", dpi = 150,
           width = width_mm, height = height_mm, units = "mm")
  invisible(file)
}

# combined multi-panel
save_fig(gear_fig, FIG, FULL_MM, 200, preview = TRUE)

# individual panels, all at the 84 mm column width; heights differ only because
# the panels carry different numbers of categories
panels <- list(
  list(p = pA, suffix = "A_design",        h = 92),
  list(p = pB, suffix = "B_raw_cpue",      h = 78),
  list(p = pC, suffix = "C_balance",      h = 105),
  list(p = pD, suffix = "D_rate_ratio",    h = 85),   # 3-line model labels
  list(p = pE, suffix = "E_adjusted_cpue", h = 78)
)

walk(panels, ~ save_fig(.x$p, sprintf("%s_%s", FIG, .x$suffix),
                        COL_MM, .x$h, preview = TRUE))

list.files("output_figs", pattern = "gear_efficiency", full.names = TRUE)
```

# 7. (moved)

The covariate correlation matrices are in `04_diagnostics/covariate_correlations_by_water_year.Rmd`.

# 8. Gear comparison for FORK LENGTH

Same question as section 3, different response: does gear type shift measured
fork length once the other predictors are accounted for?

Model structure follows `tidal-parr-forklength-analysis2_kfold.Rmd`
(`build_fl_formula()`): `ForkLength ~ <fixef> + water_year_day_z +
(1|StationCode)`, `gaussian()`, with `fl_priors`. Added covariates per request:
outflow (`out30_z`), water depth (`start_depth_z`) and a week random intercept.

One structural improvement over the catch models: fork length is measured **per
fish**, and several fish share a tow, so `(1|StationCode)` is a genuine
tow-level random effect here rather than the observation-level term it collapsed
to in section 3.

## 8.1 Paired subset

```{r fl-data}
fl <- read.csv("data/tps_forklength_data.csv") %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(SampleDate),
         yrwk = paste0(year(date), "-W", sprintf("%02d", isoweek(date))))

table(fl$Gear, fl$Water_Year)
```

Otter fork lengths exist only in WY2019, mirroring the catch data. Keep weeks in
which **both gears produced measured fish** -- a week with only one gear cannot
contribute to a within-week gear contrast.

```{r fl-subset}
fl_paired <- fl %>%
  filter(Gear %in% c("Mamou", "Otter"), Water_Year == 2019) %>%
  group_by(yrwk) %>% filter(n_distinct(Gear) == 2) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Gear = factor(Gear, levels = c("Mamou", "Otter")),
         yrwk = factor(yrwk))

fl_paired %>% group_by(Gear) %>%
  summarise(fish = n(), tows = n_distinct(StationCode),
            mean_FL = mean(ForkLength), sd_FL = sd(ForkLength),
            min = min(ForkLength), max = max(ForkLength), .groups = "drop")
```

The confounding is severe and worth seeing before any model runs:

```{r fl-confound}
# raw, all WY2019 fish (what a naive comparison would use)
fl %>% filter(Gear %in% c("Mamou","Otter"), Water_Year == 2019) %>%
  group_by(Gear) %>% summarise(n = n(), mean_FL = mean(ForkLength), .groups="drop")

# per week, shared weeks only
fl_paired %>% group_by(yrwk, Gear) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(ForkLength), sd = sd(ForkLength), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gear, values_from = c(n, mean, sd))

# same fish, centred within week -- the week effect removed by subtraction
fl_paired %>% group_by(yrwk) %>% mutate(fl_c = ForkLength - mean(ForkLength)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% group_by(Gear) %>% summarise(mean_centred = mean(fl_c), .groups = "drop")
```

Across all WY2019 fish Mamou averages **66.2 mm** and Otter **48.9 mm** -- a
17.3 mm gap. Restricting to shared weeks cuts it to 6.2 mm, and centring within
week cuts it to **about 3.9 mm**. Almost the entire apparent gear difference is
seasonal growth: Otter's fish are concentrated in W10-W16 while Mamou also fished
W18-W22, by which time the fish are much larger. Any gear conclusion drawn
without week control is measuring the calendar, not the net.

## 8.2 Models

```{r fl-models}
fl_priors <- c(set_prior("normal(0,5)", class = "b"))   # from the kfold script

fl_m1 <- fit_cached_fl("fl_m1_requested",
  ForkLength ~ Gear + out30_z + start_depth_z + water_year_day_z + (1 | StationCode),
  data = fl_paired)

fl_m2 <- fit_cached_fl("fl_m2_within_week",
  ForkLength ~ Gear + start_depth_z + (1 | yrwk) + (1 | StationCode),
  data = fl_paired)

fl_m3 <- fit_cached_fl("fl_m3_spatial",
  ForkLength ~ Gear + out30_z + start_depth_z + distance_m_z +
               distance_along_channel_z + water_year_day_z + (1 | StationCode),
  data = fl_paired)

summary(fl_m2)
```

## 8.3 A more informative model: does gear change the size *distribution*?

**This is the part I would actually rely on.** A mean-only model asks whether
one net catches bigger fish on average. That is not the question that matters
for a fork-length analysis -- gear selectivity acts on the *shape* of the size
distribution. A net with a larger mesh or a faster tow speed can return a mean
close to the other net while systematically truncating one tail.

The raw numbers already hint at this: within shared weeks the Mamou SD is
19.6 mm against Otter's 14.1 mm, a 40% difference in spread against a ~4 mm
difference in centre. A location-only model is blind to that.

`fl_m4` models the residual SD as a function of gear as well as the mean, so
`sigma_GearOtter` is the log ratio of Otter's size spread to Mamou's.

```{r fl-m4}
fl_m4 <- fit_cached_fl("fl_m4_distributional",
  bf(ForkLength ~ Gear + start_depth_z + (1 | yrwk) + (1 | StationCode),
     sigma      ~ Gear),
  data   = fl_paired,
  priors = c(set_prior("normal(0,5)", class = "b"),
             set_prior("normal(0,1)", class = "b", dpar = "sigma")))

summary(fl_m4)
```

## 8.4 Gear effect across models

```{r fl-effects}
fl_effect <- function(fit, label) {
  d <- as_draws_df(fit)$b_GearOtter
  tibble(model = label, median_mm = median(d),
         lo95 = quantile(d, .025), hi95 = quantile(d, .975),
         P_Otter_smaller = mean(d < 0))
}

bind_rows(
  fl_effect(fl_m1, "M1 requested (out30 + depth + day)"),
  fl_effect(fl_m2, "M2 within-week"),
  fl_effect(fl_m3, "M3 + spatial"),
  fl_effect(fl_m4, "M4 distributional (mean part)")
) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 2)))

# scale effect: ratio of Otter SD to Mamou SD
sig <- exp(as_draws_df(fl_m4)$b_sigma_GearOtter)
tibble(quantity = "sigma ratio (Otter / Mamou)",
       median = median(sig), lo95 = quantile(sig, .025),
       hi95 = quantile(sig, .975), P_ratio_lt_1 = mean(sig < 1)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3)))
```

A distribution-free check on the same question, with the week effect removed by
centring:

```{r fl-ks}
cw <- fl_paired %>% group_by(yrwk) %>%
  mutate(fl_c = ForkLength - mean(ForkLength)) %>% ungroup()
suppressWarnings(
  ks.test(cw$fl_c[cw$Gear == "Mamou"], cw$fl_c[cw$Gear == "Otter"])
)
```

## 8.5 Figures

```{r fl-panels}
FLFIG <- "output_figs/gear_forklength_mamou_vs_otter"

# A. design: measured fish per week per gear
fl_wk <- fl %>% filter(Gear %in% c("Mamou","Otter"), Water_Year == 2019) %>%
  count(yrwk, Gear) %>% complete(yrwk, Gear, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(yrwk) %>% mutate(both = all(n > 0)) %>% ungroup()

fA <- ggplot(fl_wk, aes(n, yrwk, fill = Gear)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = distinct(fl_wk, yrwk, both) %>% filter(!both),
            aes(x = max(fl_wk$n) * 1.03, y = yrwk, label = "no paired catch"),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 2.3, colour = "grey45",
            fontface = "italic") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GEAR_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.38))) +
  labs(title = "A. Measured fish per week", x = "Fish measured", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Excluded = one gear caught no fish (it may still have been fished)")

# B. the confounding: fish grow through the season
fB <- ggplot(filter(fl, Gear %in% c("Mamou","Otter"), Water_Year == 2019),
             aes(date, ForkLength, colour = Gear)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GEAR_COLS) +
  labs(title = "B. Season, not gear", x = "Sample date", y = "Fork length (mm)",
       subtitle = "Otter's fish are early-season; Mamou also fished W18-W22")

# C. within-week centred distributions -- the selectivity question
cw <- fl_paired %>% group_by(yrwk) %>%
  mutate(fl_c = ForkLength - mean(ForkLength)) %>% ungroup()

fC <- ggplot(cw, aes(fl_c, colour = Gear)) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GEAR_COLS) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "C. Size distribution, week removed",
       subtitle = "ECDF of fork length centred within week",
       x = "Fork length - week mean (mm)", y = "Cumulative proportion")

# D. mean gear effect across models
fl_rr <- bind_rows(
  tibble(model = "M1 requested",     d = as_draws_df(fl_m1)$b_GearOtter),
  tibble(model = "M2 within-week",   d = as_draws_df(fl_m2)$b_GearOtter),
  tibble(model = "M3 + spatial",     d = as_draws_df(fl_m3)$b_GearOtter),
  tibble(model = "M4 distributional",d = as_draws_df(fl_m4)$b_GearOtter)
) %>% mutate(model = fct_rev(fct_inorder(model)))

fD <- ggplot(fl_rr, aes(d, model)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), fill = "#7F9CB5", point_size = 1.6,
               interval_size_range = c(0.5, 1.2)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "D. Mean fork-length difference",
       subtitle = "Otter minus Mamou; dashed line = no gear effect",
       x = "Difference (mm)", y = NULL)

# E. scale effect -- the part a mean-only model cannot see
fE <- tibble(ratio = exp(as_draws_df(fl_m4)$b_sigma_GearOtter)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(ratio, "")) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), fill = "#B58F7F", point_size = 1.6,
               interval_size_range = c(0.5, 1.2)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "E. Size-spread ratio (M4)",
       subtitle = "Otter SD / Mamou SD; < 1 = Otter returns a narrower size range",
       x = "sigma ratio", y = NULL)
```

```{r fl-combined, fig.width=6.85, fig.height=7.9}
# B and C carry colour scales whose keys won't merge with A's fill keys, so the
# collected strip would show the gear legend three times; A's serves the figure.
fBb <- fB + guides(colour = "none")
fCb <- fC + guides(colour = "none")

fl_fig <- (fA | fBb) / (fCb | fD) / fE +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 0.7), guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "top")

fl_fig <- fl_fig + plot_annotation(
  title = "Mamou vs Otter: fork length, TPS WY2019",
  subtitle = "75 measured fish across 5 weeks in which both gears caught fish",
  caption = "Mean fork length differs by 17.3 mm across all WY2019 fish; within week the difference is ~4 mm.",
  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
                plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
                plot.caption = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey40", hjust = 0)))
fl_fig
```

```{r fl-save}
save_fig(fl_fig, FLFIG, FULL_MM, 200, preview = TRUE)

fl_panels <- list(
  list(p = fA, suffix = "A_design",       h = 78),
  list(p = fB, suffix = "B_season",       h = 78),
  list(p = fC, suffix = "C_ecdf",         h = 78),
  list(p = fD, suffix = "D_mean_effect",  h = 78),
  list(p = fE, suffix = "E_sigma_ratio",  h = 60)
)
walk(fl_panels, ~ save_fig(.x$p, sprintf("%s_%s", FLFIG, .x$suffix),
                           COL_MM, .x$h, preview = TRUE))
list.files("output_figs", pattern = "gear_forklength", full.names = TRUE)
```
